Definition: a particle of affirmation, surely; hence (by limitation) only
BiblicalUsage: A small word that does big work — only, surely, truly. Noah only remained alive after the flood; David says Truly my soul waiteth upon God; Moses says Only ye shall not eat the blood.
TheologicalSignificance: A particle of only and surely carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is in the mouths that say it, Noah's only, David's truly, and the certainty of a soul that has settled.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
